title: Costs and Calculations
lessons/forex-u3-l1/steps/0/title: The real cost of the spread
lessons/forex-u3-l1/steps/0/body: You see the spread in pips, but it comes out of your account in **dollars**: **cost = spread (pips) × pip value**. Pip value depends on your size, so the bigger your position, the bigger the spread cost.
lessons/forex-u3-l1/steps/1/prompt: The GBP/USD spread is 2 pips and you trade 0.5 lot. What's the spread cost?
lessons/forex-u3-l1/steps/1/explanation: The second currency in GBP/USD is the dollar, so with 0.5 lot each pip is $5. 2 pips × $5 = $10.
lessons/forex-u3-l1/steps/2/body: Some accounts (usually **ECN** or **Raw**) have a very low spread but charge a fixed **commission** per lot, for example $7 to open and close (round trip). To compare two accounts, always work out the **total cost**.
lessons/forex-u3-l1/steps/3/prompt: ECN account: 0.3-pip spread and a $6 round-trip commission per lot. What's the total cost for 2 lots of EUR/USD?
lessons/forex-u3-l1/steps/4/statement: The spread is always fixed and doesn't change when big news comes out.
lessons/forex-u3-l1/steps/4/explanation: Most accounts have floating spreads. During news, quiet hours and the reopening after a market break, the spread can grow several times wider.
lessons/forex-u3-l1/steps/5/body: If you hold a position through **rollover** (usually 5 PM New York time), you earn or pay a swap based on the **interest rate difference between the two currencies**. At most brokers, currency swaps are **tripled on Wednesday** to cover the weekend.
lessons/forex-u3-l1/steps/5/tip: Swap-free (Islamic) accounts have no swap, but some brokers charge a different fee instead.
lessons/forex-u3-l1/steps/6/prompt: You opened a position on Monday and closed it Friday before rollover, so it went through 4 rollovers, Monday to Thursday. Each rollover costs $3 in swap, and Wednesday's is tripled. What's the total swap?
lessons/forex-u3-l1/steps/6/explanation: Monday 3 + Tuesday 3 + Wednesday 9 + Thursday 3 = $18. Wednesday's triple swap also covers Saturday and Sunday.
lessons/forex-u3-l1/steps/7/pairs/2/mean: Interest for holding a position overnight
lessons/forex-u3-l1/steps/7/pairs/3/mean: When the daily swap is charged
lessons/forex-u3-l1/steps/8/sentence: Scalpers mostly worry about the ___, but swing traders who hold positions for several nights also need to count the ___.
lessons/forex-u3-l1/steps/8/explanation: A scalper takes lots of short trades and pays the spread every time. A swing trader trades less, but every night a position stays open comes with a swap.
lessons/forex-u3-l2/title: Pip value and profit and loss
lessons/forex-u3-l2/steps/0/body: **Pip value = pip size × number of units**, and the answer is in the **second (quote) currency**. In EUR/USD the second currency is the dollar, so for 1 lot: 0.0001 × 100,000 = **$10**. The same number works for every pair whose second currency is USD.
lessons/forex-u3-l2/steps/1/prompt: You're trading 0.3 lot on AUD/USD. What's each pip worth?
lessons/forex-u3-l2/steps/1/explanation: The second currency in AUD/USD is the dollar, so 1 lot = $10 per pip, and 0.3 lot = $3.
lessons/forex-u3-l2/steps/2/title: When the second currency isn't the dollar
lessons/forex-u3-l2/steps/2/body: In **USD/JPY** a pip is 0.01, so for 1 lot: 0.01 × 100,000 = **1,000 yen**. To convert to dollars, divide by the USD/JPY price: at 150, each pip is about **$6.67**, and it shifts a little as the price moves.
lessons/forex-u3-l2/steps/3/statement: For 1 lot, a pip is worth exactly $10 in every currency pair.
lessons/forex-u3-l2/steps/3/explanation: It's exactly $10 only when the second currency is the dollar (like EUR/USD) and your account is in dollars. In USD/JPY at 150, for example, it's about $6.67.
lessons/forex-u3-l2/steps/4/prompt: You bought 0.5 lot at 1.0850. If price hits your take profit at 1.0890, how much do you make?
lessons/forex-u3-l2/steps/4/explanation: 1.0890 − 1.0850 = 40 pips. With 0.5 lot each pip is $5, so 40 × 5 = $200. If your stop loss had been hit, you'd have lost 20 pips × 5 = $100.
lessons/forex-u3-l2/steps/5/title: Size your trade from your risk
lessons/forex-u3-l2/steps/5/body: Once you know the pip value: **size (lots) = risk amount ÷ (stop loss pips × pip value of 1 lot)**. That way, if your stop loss is hit, you lose exactly the amount you chose beforehand.
lessons/forex-u3-l2/steps/6/prompt: Your account is $5,000 and you want to risk 1%. Your stop loss on EUR/USD is 20 pips. What's the right size?
lessons/forex-u3-l2/steps/6/explanation: 1% of 5,000 = $50. 50 ÷ (20 × 10) = 0.25 lot. If your stop loss is hit: 20 pips × $2.50 = a $50 loss.
lessons/forex-u3-l2/steps/7/sentence: In USD/JPY one pip equals ___, and for 1 lot each pip is worth ___ yen.
lessons/forex-u3-l2/steps/7/explanation: Yen pairs have two decimals, so a pip is 0.01, and 0.01 × 100,000 = 1,000 yen.
lessons/forex-u3-l2/steps/8/prompt: You sold 1 lot of USD/JPY at 150.00 and closed at 149.40. Roughly how much did you make?
lessons/forex-u3-l2/steps/8/explanation: 150.00 − 149.40 = 60 pips; 60 × 1,000 yen = 60,000 yen. Divided by 149.40, that's about $402. You were short and price fell, so it's a profit.
lessons/forex-u3-l3/steps/0/body: **Required margin = position value ÷ leverage**. 1 lot of EUR/USD at 1.0850 is worth $108,500. With 1:100 leverage, your broker locks **$1,085** of your account as margin.
lessons/forex-u3-l3/steps/1/prompt: You open 0.5 lot of GBP/USD at 1.2700 with 1:50 leverage. What's the required margin?
lessons/forex-u3-l3/steps/1/explanation: Position value = 50,000 pounds × 1.2700 = $63,500. Divided by 50, that's $1,270.
lessons/forex-u3-l3/steps/2/body: **Equity** is your balance plus your floating profit or loss. **Margin level = equity ÷ used margin × 100%**. The bigger your floating loss, the lower this percentage goes.
lessons/forex-u3-l3/steps/3/prompt: Your equity is $1,500 and your used margin is $500. What's your margin level?
lessons/forex-u3-l3/steps/3/explanation: 1,500 ÷ 500 × 100% = 300%. The higher this number, the further you are from a margin call.
lessons/forex-u3-l3/steps/4/body: Every broker has two limits. For example, when your margin level hits **100%**, you get a **margin call** (a warning, and usually no new trades), and if it hits **50%**, a **stop out** happens: the broker closes your positions itself, usually starting with the biggest loser.
lessons/forex-u3-l3/steps/4/tip: These percentages differ between brokers. Check them in your broker's agreement or on its website.
lessons/forex-u3-l3/steps/5/statement: In a stop out, the broker closes your positions itself, even if you don't want it to.
lessons/forex-u3-l3/steps/5/explanation: A stop out is automatic and exists to keep your account from going negative. It's not your call, which is why you should have exited with a stop loss long before.
lessons/forex-u3-l3/steps/6/prompt: Your balance is $1,000, you bought 0.5 lot of EUR/USD, and your used margin is $540. Your broker's stop out is 50%. Roughly how many pips against you will trigger the stop out?
lessons/forex-u3-l3/steps/6/explanation: Stop out means equity = 50% × 540 = $270. So the loss = 1,000 − 270 = $730, and 730 ÷ 5 = 146 pips. (92 pips is where the 100% margin call hits.)
lessons/forex-u3-l3/steps/7/prompt: Same position: bought at 1.0800. Tap the candle where the position got stopped out.
lessons/forex-u3-l3/steps/7/explanation: The first time a candle's low reached 1.0654, equity fell to 50% of margin and the broker closed the position. The painful part: price bounced back afterward, but the position was already closed.
lessons/forex-u3-l3/steps/8/prompt: When a position's loss grows, in what order do these things happen?
lessons/forex-u3-l3/steps/8/items/2: Margin level reaches the margin call limit
lessons/forex-u3-l3/steps/8/items/3: At the stop out level, the broker closes the position
lessons/forex-u3-l3/steps/8/explanation: A floating loss comes straight out of your equity, and your margin level drops: first the warning (margin call), then the forced close (stop out).
lessons/forex-u3-l3/steps/9/sentence: To stay away from a stop out, use less ___ and always set a ___.
lessons/forex-u3-l3/steps/9/explanation: Less leverage means less margin for your size, and a stop loss gets you out of the trade long before a margin call.
